To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the aspect ratio of a shape is processed at a different stage of visual processing than its orientation and (2) this is due to the fact that the former requires the processing of boundary information and the latter requires the processing of body information.
the visual system uses the information from body and boundary to compute the visual aspect ratio, and that the two sources of information are integrated at a very early stage of the visual system.

the visual processing of the aspect ratio of an object depends on the relative position of the object in the visual field, and that these two sources of information (boundary information and body information) are combined to form a single representation of the shape of an object.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether or not there is a single visual mechanism that is sensitive to the aspect ratio of an object's shape.
understanding the role of the boundary and body information of a shape in visual processing.
the convergence of body and boundary information in the visual perception of aspect ratio.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the visual system is sensitive to the aspect ratio of a shape, but the exact nature of the underlying mechanism is unclear.

the human visual system is capable of extracting the aspect ratio of a 2-D object in a very short time, even if it is presented in a cluttered scene, and even if it is partially occluded by other objects.
the visual processing of the aspect ratio of objects is a function of both body and boundary information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the visual processing of the aspect ratio of an object is based on both boundary and body information.
the visual system uses information about the boundary of a stimulus to determine the aspect ratio of the stimulus.
the brain uses both the body and the boundary information to estimate the aspect ratio of an object.
The main takeaway from our work is that
visual processing of aspect ratios in 2D objects (e.g., rectangles, squares) is a function of both the object's boundary and its internal body.
the visual system can extract information about aspect ratio (AR) from the boundary of an object and that the visual system uses this information to guide the perception of AR.
the visual system uses both boundary and body cues to estimate aspect ratio.
